items.summary: Skill libraries, curated skill lists and Claude Code skills for diagrams, second brains and content, feeding skill authoring and diagram tooling.

items.summary: Retrieval, memory, ontologies, LLM data processing, inference and ML models for building knowledge-grounded AI apps and pipelines.

items.summary: Django ecosystem, ERP and business app frameworks, admin widgets, Postgres and deployment for the Python backend projects.

ideas: Borrow its lesson progression for godotgo onboarding
Reference it as learning material in godotgo docs
GDQuest/learn-gdscript.summary: Interactive in-browser course that teaches Godot's GDScript from zero, free and built with Godot.
GDQuest/learn-gdscript.why: Strong GDScript teaching content and a model for in-engine interactive lessons, though its license is 'other' so reuse needs checking.

ideas: Reuse its skill layout and prompt structure
Produce HTML explainers with embedded diagrams
Apply its writing-style constraints (ST E100) to skill output
QingYunA/answer-me-with-html.summary: An agent skill that has AI agents answer complex questions with a readable one-page HTML explainer.
QingYunA/answer-me-with-html.why: It is a compact example of a Claude Code skill that produces HTML explainers. The skill structure and its output conventions are worth borrowing.

ideas: Mine it for skills worth adding or adapting
Check skills against its cross-tool compatibility
Submit the fleet's own skills for listing
VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills.summary: A curated list of more than 1000 agent skills from official teams and the community, for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor.
VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills.why: It is a large, active index of agent skills across tools. It works as a discovery source and a benchmark for the skills repo.

ideas: Borrow its CV and publications collection layout
Reuse its author sidebar profile pattern
academicpages/academicpages.github.io.summary: GitHub Pages Jekyll template for personal and academic portfolio websites written in HTML and Markdown.
academicpages/academicpages.github.io.why: Its portfolio page structure for CV, publications and talks maps onto the personal portfolio site, without needing a full switch.

ideas: Align SKILL.md frontmatter and layout with the official spec
Port useful reference skills into the fleet's skills repo
Use its skill-creator pattern to validate new skills
anthropics/skills.summary: Anthropic's official public repository of Agent Skills, with reference skill implementations and the skill format used by Claude.
anthropics/skills.why: Canonical source for the Agent Skills format and examples; the skills project should follow its structure and conventions directly.

ideas: Add official tech logos to generated architecture diagrams
Copy its one-sentence-to-diagram skill prompt design
caru-ini/stack-diagram.summary: Agent skill that turns a one-sentence stack description into an architecture diagram using official technology logos.
caru-ini/stack-diagram.why: Closely matches archify's diagram-agent scope; its official-logo approach and skill packaging are worth borrowing.

ideas: Copy the Docker Compose layout for Dagster with dbt and DuckDB
Wire dbt models into Dagster assets
Add a Superset layer for BI dashboards
cnstlungu/portable-data-stack-dagster.summary: A portable datamart and BI stack built with Docker, Dagster, dbt, DuckDB and Superset.
cnstlungu/portable-data-stack-dagster.why: Its stack overlaps strongly with edgar-pipeline (Dagster, dbt, DuckDB). It is a good reference for Docker packaging and for how the layers connect.

ideas: Define sensor nodes with declarative YAML configs
Borrow its component and platform abstraction
Add OTA update and MQTT discovery conventions
esphome/esphome.summary: A system that configures ESP32, ESP8266 and RP2040 devices from YAML files and connects them to home automation systems and MQTT.
esphome/esphome.why: It covers the same ground as sensor-mesh (ESP32, MQTT, PlatformIO). Its YAML-driven device config and component model are worth borrowing.

ideas: Define content types and front matter schemas to drive editing forms
Add a content dashboard listing drafts and published pages
Use a VS Code webview panel for a CMS UI
estruyf/vscode-front-matter.summary: A VS Code extension that works as a CMS for Markdown content in static site generators such as Jekyll, Hugo and Next.js.
estruyf/vscode-front-matter.why: It is a mature in-editor CMS for Markdown and Jekyll content. zer0-CMS can borrow its content-model and editor UX ideas without adopting the whole extension.

gkd-kit/gkd.summary: Android app that automates screen taps using accessibility services, selectors and subscription rules, built with Kotlin and Compose.
gkd-kit/gkd.why: Android accessibility auto-clicker is outside the fleet's needs; GPL-3.0 licence also limits reuse of its code.

ideas: Add an Alloy service to the docker-compose stack
Define pipelines scraping Prometheus targets and shipping logs to Loki
Use its OTLP receivers for app traces
grafana/alloy.summary: Grafana's OpenTelemetry Collector distribution with programmable pipelines for metrics, logs and traces.
grafana/alloy.why: Fits fleet-observe's Grafana, Prometheus and OpenTelemetry stack as the collector that feeds Prometheus, Loki and Tempo.

ideas: Use it as a remote-write target if metric retention grows
Reference its OTLP ingestion setup
grafana/mimir.summary: Horizontally scalable, highly available, multi-tenant long-term storage for Prometheus metrics, with OTLP support.
grafana/mimir.why: It is a heavyweight, AGPL-licensed storage backend that is overkill for a small fleet stack today. It becomes relevant if fleet-observe needs long-term metrics retention.

ideas: Browse its skill structure for patterns worth copying
janestreet/agent_skills.summary: Jane Street's collection of agent skills, with no description or topics beyond the name.
janestreet/agent_skills.why: Popular and from a respected engineering firm, but the data gives no description or topics, so its content and scope are unclear.

ideas: Track Jekyll releases to keep the theme compatible
Use the Jekyll plugin and Liquid docs to improve theme features
jekyll/jekyll.summary: A blog-aware static site generator written in Ruby, with Markdown and Liquid templating.
jekyll/jekyll.why: Jekyll is the core engine under zer0-mistakes and the other Jekyll sites in the fleet. Tracking upstream keeps them compatible and current.

ideas: Borrow its client-side search implementation
Adopt its nested navigation and collapsible sidebar approach
Reuse its callout and label components
just-the-docs/just-the-docs.summary: Highly customizable, responsive Jekyll theme for documentation sites with built-in search.
just-the-docs/just-the-docs.why: A mature Jekyll docs theme; zer0-mistakes can borrow its navigation, search and callout patterns rather than replace its own theme.

ideas: Study its skin and color-scheme switching
Review its layout options for blog and docs
kitian616/jekyll-TeXt-theme.summary: Highly customizable Jekyll theme for personal sites, blogs, projects and documentation.
kitian616/jekyll-TeXt-theme.why: Feature-rich theme worth studying, but the last push was June 2026, so it is less active than other Jekyll options.

ideas: Study its module layout for shared Compose code
Borrow its GitHub releases API client patterns
komi-store/komi-store.summary: Open-source Kotlin Multiplatform app store for installing developers' releases from GitHub, Codeberg and Forgejo.
komi-store/komi-store.why: A large, real Compose Multiplatform codebase that shows structure for shared UI across Android and desktop; the app itself isn't needed.

ideas: Validate generated diagrams with the mermaid parser
Use architecture and C4 diagram types for system-design output
Embed rendering in docs sites via mermaid.js
mermaid-js/mermaid.summary: JavaScript/TypeScript library that renders flowcharts, sequence diagrams, mindmaps and more from markdown-like text definitions.
mermaid-js/mermaid.why: Archify is built on Mermaid diagrams-as-code; this is the upstream renderer and syntax authority, already starred.

ideas: Compare its search options (Lunr and Algolia) with the zer0-mistakes search
Reuse its layout and author-profile patterns
Follow its theme-gem packaging and upgrade documentation
mmistakes/minimal-mistakes.summary: A popular Jekyll theme for personal sites, blogs, documentation and portfolios, packaged as a Ruby gem with Algolia and Lunr search.
mmistakes/minimal-mistakes.why: It is a mature Jekyll theme with the same gem packaging and similar goals as zer0-mistakes. It is useful as a reference for layouts, search and docs rather than as a replacement.

ideas: Borrow its default alert thresholds and health templates
Use its per-second dashboard layout for fleet-observe panels
netdata/netdata.summary: A full-stack observability platform covering metrics, logs, traces, flows and AI-assisted SRE, with OpenTelemetry support.
netdata/netdata.why: It is a large, GPL-licensed all-in-one monitoring product. fleet-observe can borrow dashboard and alerting ideas, but should not adopt it over Grafana and Prometheus.

ideas: Merge upstream installer and migration scripts into amrchy
Take its theme-switching mechanism
Copy its keybinding and default config conventions
omacom/omarchy.summary: An opinionated, modern Linux setup built mostly in shell, based on Arch and Hyprland.
omacom/omarchy.why: amrchy appears to be an Omarchy-style Arch and Hyprland fork. Following upstream keeps its dotfiles, scripts and themes current.

ideas: Track OSC protocol and CLI changes that affect the extension
Check new language features for syntax highlighting
sonic-pi-net/sonic-pi.summary: A live-coding music environment for making sound with code, aimed at education and performance.
sonic-pi-net/sonic-pi.why: It is the upstream project that the vs-sonic-pi extension targets. Watch it for changes to its OSC and server interface that could break the extension.

ideas: Pick networking, storage and navigation libs for fleet-mobile
Check it for Compose Multiplatform UI components
terrakok/kmp-awesome.summary: Curated awesome list of Kotlin Multiplatform libraries, tools and resources.
terrakok/kmp-awesome.why: A useful catalogue for picking KMP and Compose Multiplatform libraries, but it is a reference list, not something to depend on.

ideas: Model flexible page content as StreamField-style blocks
Copy its page tree and draft-and-publish workflow
Look at its admin editing UX
wagtail/wagtail.summary: A Django content management system focused on flexibility and editor experience.
wagtail/wagtail.why: zer0-CMS has Wagtail and Django in its topics. Wagtail is the reference implementation for StreamField-style flexible content and editor UX.
